newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NEW EPISODE OF BRUSSELS BOURSE GOOD NEWS SHOW.
newsitem.headline: NEW EPISODE OF BRUSSELS BOURSE GOOD NEWS SHOW.

text.p: Belgian shares, oblivious of any news that might undermine bullish sentiment, soared to new highs on Thursday with hardly any doubt in players' minds that the record run could end soon.
"The market is as solid as a rock. It's just buy, buy, buy and no-one around to sell," one trader said.
At 0900 GMT, the Bel-20 index of leading shares was up 18.61 points, or 0.79 percent, at a record 2,381.31.
The flavour of the day was retailer Colruyt which dealers said was being fired on by its inclusion in a major European investment fund.
Colruyt, which already rose 2.4 percent on Wednesday, was up 5.6 percent at 15,875 francs. The company is expected to publish annual results on June 25.
"We may now well have reached the stage of exaggeration," one trader said about the Bel-20's continuing surge.
Dealers said many shares were expensive but were driven up further by speculation.

Chemicals and drugs company UCB was seen as one of the exceptions to the rule and continued to enjoy buy or hold recommendations. UCB, the star of business on Wednesday with a 10.9 percent leap, added a further 4.9 percent at 117,300
UCB has been shooting up in recent days after breaching the 100,000-franc barrier and is lifted mainly by a strong profit rise forecast and expectations of a stock split.
"In price/earnings terms, it is expensive, although officially we still have it on our buy list," one trader said.
But he warned that UCB was depending heavily on star products Zyrtec and Nootropil -- anti-allergy and cerebral dysfunction treatment drugs respectively.
"If something were to go wrong with one of these two drugs, UCB's share price is bound to collapse," he said.
